case_studies.title: AI Prototyper: A Figma Plugin for Decomposition-Based GUI Prototyping with LLMs
case_studies.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) prototyping remains a time-consuming activity that demands both design expertise and considerable manual effort. As GUI prototypes are non-code artifacts that evolve alongside requirements throughout the development cycle, automating their generation is directly relevant to software maintenance and evolution. We present AI Prototyper, an open-source Figma plugin that automates GUI prototyping through a decomposition and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline. Given a natural-language description of a desired screen, such as a login page or a product detail
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of time-consuming GUI prototyping by building an AI-powered Figma plugin that automates the process, resulting in faster and more efficient prototype generation. The plugin, called AI Prototyper, uses natural-language descriptions to generate GUI prototypes. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: DataShield: Uncovering Risky Fine-Tuning Data Across LLMs Through Consensus Subspace Alignment
case_studies.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on domain-specific datasets has become a standard paradigm for adapting LLMs to specialized applications. However, recent work has shown that even fine-tuning on benign task-specific data can substantially weaken the safety capabilities of LLMs. While existing efforts have made progress in identifying data responsible for safety degradation, they usually rely on a single mean vector computed over a specific model with its tokenizer to represent the safety direction, which limits both the effectiveness and transferability of their risk assessment measure
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of identifying risky data used to fine-tune large language models, which can weaken their safety capabilities. The researchers built DataShield, a system that uses consensus subspace alignment to uncover such data. The result is a more effective and transferable risk assessment measure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI or machine learning infrastructure, check your fine-tuning data pipelines for potential safety risks: step 1, review your data sources and quality controls, step 2, assess the potential impact on your LLMs' safety capabilities, step 3, consider implementing DataShield or similar risk assessment measures.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Fine-tuning LLMs on domain-specific data and potential risks in safety capabilities.

case_studies.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
case_studies.abstract: Traffic agencies now have access to large volumes of video-derived data for studying safety and congestion. Most of these data are observational and collected without interventions, which makes causal questions such as "How would rain change traffic density?" difficult to answer. We present teLLMe, a system for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving datasets. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of analyzing the cause-and-effect relationships in urban driving data, the team built a system called teLLMe for exploratory causal analysis, and the result is a more accurate understanding of how different factors like rain affect traffic density. The system uses video-derived data and machine learning algorithms to answer causal questions. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Enhancing Small Language Models Reasoning through Knowledge Graph Grounding
case_studies.abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) have set benchmarks for zero-shot reasoning, their deployment remains cost-prohibitive and environmentally taxing. Small Language Models (SLMs) offer a sustainable alternative, but prone to errors, on tasks requiring complex, multi-hop logical grounding. We investigate a neuro-symbolic agentic framework to enhance the reasoning capabilities of SLMs, specifically Gemma 3 (1B, 4B) and Llama 3.2 (3B), using the CLUTRR kinship benchmark. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of small language models being prone to errors in complex reasoning tasks by building a neuro-symbolic framework to enhance their capabilities. The researchers built a framework that transforms small language models into minimalist agents with specialized tool calls. The result is improved reasoning capabilities for small language models, but this is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.
